title: Reduce embedding endpoint tail latency with microburst shaping and kernel hinting
creator: Liam Chen
description: We see intermittent p99/p999 spikes on the embeddings endpoint during bursty traffic (small requests arriving in tight bursts). Previous coalescing improvements reduced average cost but left a long tail caused by microbursts that evade the coalescer and trigger suboptimal kernel selection. This ticket implements a microburst shaping layer (short, low-latency delay + priority stacking) together with kernel-hint metadata from the scheduler so that the runtime chooses kernels optimized for short sequences and immediate drains. We will also add a tail sampler to collect request traces and a short A/B evaluation against a control to measure quality impact for reranking workloads.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p99 latency for embeddings endpoint reduced by >=20% under synthetic microburst load compared to control
p999 latency reduced by >=15% on production trace replay tests
No regression in average token throughput or error rate (<0.1% increase)
Kernel hint API defined and implemented: scheduler attaches kernel_hint tags to microburst-shaped batches
Tail sampler collecting full request -> response latency traces is enabled behind feature flag and exports to trace dashboard
tasks: Design microburst shaping algorithm and backpressure/priority rules (edge delay, max hold time, priority buckets)
Implement shaping handler in front of embedding coalescer with runtime flag
Extend scheduler to emit kernel_hint metadata (short_seq, low_batch, preemptable)
Wire kernel_hint into kernel selector to prefer low-latency kernels for flagged batches
Add tail sampler that stores 1-in-10000 embedding requests with full latency trace and KV-cache state
Create synthetic microburst load harness and production trace replay job for CI/CD performance gate
Run A/B evaluation (10% traffic) for 72 hours and gather latency/cost/quality metrics
Document configuration knobs and rollout plan in Confluence and runbook
notes: Microburst shaping is intentionally conservative: max hold time default 6ms to avoid adding visible latency to single-request flows
Kernel hints are coarse-grained tags; avoid per-request heavy metadata to keep scheduler overhead minimal
Reranking customers may see slight ranking differences if kernels quantize differently; we'll include a quality guardrail in A/B
We may later fold shaping into the coalescer once stable to reduce extra hops
Estimate assumes 2 engineers full-time for 2 sprints and 1 performance engineer for validation
comments: 2025-03-06 - Liam Chen: Spike complete. Evaluated three shaping strategies: fixed-delay, adaptive-delay by queue length, and token-window smoothing. Adaptive-delay with max 6ms and priority buckets looked best in sims.

2025-03-12 - Priya Patel (PM): Add tail sampler and production trace replay before A/B. PM request: include precision@10 measurement for reranking customers.

2025-03-14 - Diego Martinez (Perf): Kernel selector adjustment reduced per-batch switch overhead. Need to validate KV-cache interaction for shaped batches; observed occasional cache-miss amplification in replay tests.
2025-03-18 - Design review: UX for rollout flag in Console approved; default off for all tenants, opt-in via per-route setting for early customers.

2025-03-20 - Asha Verma: Canary started (5% traffic) with shaping enabled. Early telemetry: average latency unchanged, p99 improved ~22% for small-request traces. Continuing monitoring for errors and cost impact.
